note: No change at all. A request naming a room and a member and nothing to set or remove asks for nothing; `minProperties` is what refuses it, since `required` alone would accept it.
No member. The label is keyed by room AND member — a person holding one room as two personas keeps one for each — so the key holder never infers whose label is meant.
A member that is not a DID.
A detail both given and removed. dependentSchemas makes the two mutually exclusive, so a request cannot be read two ways.
removeDescription: false. Only `true` is meaningful; `false` would be a second spelling of "unchanged".
label: null. Removal is `removeLabel`, never a null, so libraries that map absent and null to one option cannot confuse "unchanged" with "remove".
An empty label. Removal is `removeLabel`; an empty string would be a third spelling of it.
A line break in the label. A name is one line; a surface listing rooms must not be made to render a second.
An escape character in the notes. Line breaks and tabs are allowed there; other control characters are not, since a terminal surface would interpret them.
An empty tag list. Removing every tag is `removeTags`; there is one way to say "none".
A repeated tag. Tags are a set.
A request to share the label. There is no such member: the label is never sent to the room, its host or a community, so no request carries a destination for it.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.
An empty personal label. A key holder holding no detail holds no label and omits `personal`; an object carrying only `updatedAt` would be a second way to say so.
No `changed`. A caller retrying a request needs to know whether this one wrote anything.
